text: I think motivations vary. Some people are driven by a sense of duty or compassion, while others see it as a way to gain experience or meet like-minded people. Interestingly, research suggests that volunteers often benefit as much as those they help, since contributing to something bigger than yourself gives life a sense of purpose. So it's rarely purely altruistic, but that doesn't make it any less valuable.

tips.example: while others see it as a way to gain experience or meet like-minded people

tips.en: A cautious conclusion avoids being absolute.
tips.example: So it's rarely purely altruistic, but that doesn't make it any less valuable

text: I wouldn't say less willing, but perhaps less aware of opportunities to help. In large cities, people tend to be absorbed in their own routines and wary of getting involved. Yet when there's a crisis, such as a natural disaster, you often see extraordinary generosity. I think it's a matter of context: when helping is made easy and visible, people respond.

tips.en: Adjusting the question shows critical thinking.
tips.example: I wouldn't say less willing, but perhaps less aware of opportunities to help
Yet when there's a crisis, such as a natural disaster, you often see extraordinary generosity

text: At the very least, citizens should respect shared spaces, follow basic regulations and take part in local decisions, for example by voting. Beyond that, there's an informal duty to look out for vulnerable neighbours. I'm not convinced these should be enforced by law, since social norms and peer pressure tend to be more effective. Laws can punish bad behaviour, but they can't create genuine goodwill.

tips.example: I'm not convinced these should be enforced by law

tips.en: A short contrast at the end works as a strong conclusion.

tips.ru: Короткое противопоставление в конце звучит как сильный вывод.
tips.example: Laws can punish bad behaviour, but they can't create genuine goodwill

text: I expect they'll become more diverse and, paradoxically, both more global and more local. Remote work could revitalise smaller towns, as people no longer need to live near their offices. Meanwhile, digital platforms make it easier to organise neighbourhood initiatives. The challenge will be ensuring that online connection supplements, rather than replaces, face-to-face interaction, which is still essential for trust.
